claim: A hallmark of aging is loss of differentiated cell identity.
source: A hallmark of aging is loss of differentiated cell identity.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about aging.

claim: Aged Drosophila midgut differentiated enterocytes (ECs) lose their identity, impairing tissue homeostasis.
source: Aged Drosophila midgut differentiated enterocytes (ECs) lose their identity, impairing tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is a general statement about the biological phenomenon being studied, supported by the research context.

claim: An RNAi screen targeting ubiquitin-related genes in ECs identified seventeen genes as identity regulators.
source: To discover identity regulators, we performed an RNAi screen targeting ubiquitin-related genes in ECs. Seventeen genes were identified, including the deubiquitinase Non-stop (CG4166).
evidence: The screen results are described in the abstract and detailed in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: Non-stop (CG4166) is a deubiquitinase identified in the screen.
source: Seventeen genes were identified, including the deubiquitinase Non-stop (CG4166).
evidence: Non-stop is explicitly identified as a deubiquitinase in the abstract.

claim: Acute loss of Non-stop in young ECs phenocopies aged ECs at cellular and tissue levels.
source: Lineage tracing established that acute loss of Non-stop in young ECs phenocopies aged ECs at cellular and tissue levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Non-stop maintains identity as part of a Non-stop identity complex (NIC) containing E(y)2, Sgf11, Cp190, (Mod) mdg4, and Nup98.
source: Proteomic analysis unveiled that Non-stop maintains identity as part of a Non-stop identity complex (NIC) containing E(y)2, Sgf11, Cp190, (Mod) mdg4, and Nup98.
evidence: Proteomic analysis identified the components of the NIC complex.

claim: Non-stop ensured chromatin accessibility, maintaining the EC-gene signature.
source: Non-stop ensured chromatin accessibility, maintaining the EC-gene signature, and protected NIC subunit stability.
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Non-stop protected NIC subunit stability.
source: Non-stop ensured chromatin accessibility, maintaining the EC-gene signature, and protected NIC subunit stability.
evidence: Protein level analysis showed that Non-stop is required for maintaining NIC subunit protein levels.

claim: Upon aging, the levels of Non-stop and NIC subunits declined.
source: Upon aging, the levels of Non-stop and NIC subunits declined, distorting the unique organization of the EC nucleus.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data in aged midguts showed reduced protein levels of Non-stop and NIC subunits.

claim: Aging distorted the unique organization of the EC nucleus.
source: Upon aging, the levels of Non-stop and NIC subunits declined, distorting the unique organization of the EC nucleus.
evidence: Microscopy data showed changes in nuclear organization markers in aged ECs.

claim: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs safeguards NIC subunits.
source: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs safeguards NIC subunits, nuclear organization, and suppressed aging phenotypes.
evidence: Overexpression experiments showed that maintaining Non-stop levels prevented decline of NIC subunits.

claim: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs safeguards nuclear organization.
source: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs safeguards NIC subunits, nuclear organization, and suppressed aging phenotypes.
evidence: Microscopy data showed that Non-stop expression restored nuclear organization markers in aged ECs.

claim: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs suppressed aging phenotypes.
source: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop in wildtype aged ECs safeguards NIC subunits, nuclear organization, and suppressed aging phenotypes.
evidence: Multiple assays including gut integrity and marker expression showed suppression of aging phenotypes.

claim: Non-stop and NIC supervise EC identity and protect from premature aging.
source: Thus, Non-stop and NIC, supervise EC identity and protects from premature aging.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Identity supervisors safeguard the expression of genes that enable differentiated cells to respond to environmental cues and perform required physiological tasks.
source: Identity supervisors safeguard the expression of genes that enable differentiated cells to respond to environmental cues and perform required physiological tasks.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about identity supervisors.

claim: Identity supervisors ensure silencing/repression of previous fate and non-relevant gene programs and reduce transcriptional noise.
source: Concomitantly, they ensure silencing/repression of previous fate and non-relevant gene programs and reduce transcriptional noise.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about identity supervisors.

claim: Inability to safeguard cell identity is a hallmark of aging and results in diseases such as neurodegeneration, diabetes, and cancer.
source: Inability to safeguard cell identity is a hallmark of aging and results in diseases such as neurodegeneration, diabetes, and cancer (Bensellam et al., 2018; Hudish et al., 2019; Conway et al., 2015; Hnisz et al., 2013; Deneris and Hobert, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Transcription factors (TFs) together with chromatin regulators and architectural/scaffold proteins establish and maintain large-scale chromatin and nuclear organization that is unique to the differentiated state of the cell.
source: In many cases, transcription factors (TFs) together with chromatin regulators and architectural/scaffold proteins establish and maintain large-scale chromatin and nuclear organization that is unique to the differentiated state of the cell (Blau and Baltimore, 1991; Booth and Brunet, 2016; Naetar et al., 2017; Bitman-Lotan and Orian, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In adult Drosophila midgut epithelia, the transcription factor Hey (Hairy/E(spl)-related with YRPW motif), together with Drosophila nuclear type A lamin, Lamin C (LamC), co-supervise identity of fully differentiated enterocytes (ECs).
source: In adult Drosophila midgut epithelia, the transcription factor Hey (Hairy/E(spl)-related with YRPW motif), together with Drosophila nuclear type A lamin, Lamin C (LamC), co-supervise identity of fully differentiated enterocytes (ECs) (Monastirioti et al., 2010; Gruenbaum and Foisner, 2015; Flint Brodsly et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Drosophila midgut epithelia intestinal stem cells (ISC) either self-renew or differentiate into progenitor cells that mature into enteroendocrine cells (EEs) or give rise to enteroblast (EB) progenitors.
source: Highly similar to the vertebrate gut, Drosophila midgut epithelia intestinal stem cells (ISC) either self-renew or differentiate into progenitor cells that mature into enteroendocrine cells (EEs) or give rise to enteroblast (EB) progenitors.
evidence: This describes the established differentiation pathway in the Drosophila midgut.

claim: EBs mature into fully polyploid differentiated enterocytes (ECs) that carry out many critical physiological tasks of the intestine.
source: EBs mature into fully polyploid differentiated enterocytes (ECs) that carry out many critical physiological tasks of the intestine (Figure 1A; Jiang and Edgar, 2012; Lemaitre and Miguel-Aliaga, 2013; Buchon et al., 2013; Hung et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the established differentiation pathway in the Drosophila midgut, supported by citations and Figure 1A.

claim: Aging affects the entire midgut, and is associated with loss of EC identity, mis-differentiation of progenitors, pathological activation of the immune system, and loss of the physiological properties of the gut and its integrity.
source: Aging affects the entire midgut, and is associated with loss of EC identity, mis-differentiation of progenitors, pathological activation of the immune system, and loss of the physiological properties of the gut and its integrity.
evidence: This statement summarizes known effects of aging on the Drosophila midgut.

claim: Aging results in loss of intestinal compartmentalization, and microbiota-dysbiosis, all leading to reduced lifespan.
source: It also results in loss of intestinal compartmentalization, and microbiota-dysbiosis, all leading to reduced lifespan (Biteau et al., 2010; Rera et al., 2012; Bonnay et al., 2013; Ferrandon, 2013; Chen et al., 2014; Rodriguez-Fernandez et al., 2020; Jasper, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research on aging in the Drosophila midgut.

claim: During aging, the protein levels of identity supervisors such as Hey and LamC decline, resulting in inability to maintain EC-gene programs and ectopic expression of previous- and non-relevant gene programs.
source: During aging, the protein levels of identity supervisors such as Hey and LamC decline, resulting in inability to maintain EC-gene programs and ectopic expression of previous- and non-relevant gene programs (Neves et al., 2015; Takeda et al., 2018; Flint Brodsly et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Continuous expression of Hey in aged ECs restores and protects EC identity, gut integrity, and tissue homeostasis.
source: Indeed, continuous expression of Hey in aged ECs restores and protects EC identity, gut integrity, and tissue homeostasis (Flint Brodsly et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: An RNAi screen was performed to search for Ub/UbL-related genes within ECs that supervise identity.
source: We performed an RNAi screen to search for Ub/UbL-related genes within ECs that supervise identity.
evidence: The screen methodology is described in the manuscript.

claim: Screening of 362 genes identified 17 genes whose conditional elimination in fully differentiated ECs resulted in loss of EC identity.
source: Screening of 362 genes, 17 were identified whose conditional elimination in fully differentiated ECs resulted in loss of EC identity.
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: The deubiquitinating isopeptidase (DUB) Non-stop (Non-stop/dUSP22) is a key EC identity supervisor.
source: Further analysis revealed one of them, the deubiquitinating isopeptidase (DUB) Non-stop (Non-stop/dUSP22) is a key EC identity supervisor.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the screen results and subsequent analysis.

claim: Purification and proteomic analysis identified Non-stop as part of a CP190/Nup98/Sgf11/e(y)2/mdg4 protein complex, termed Non-stop identity complex (NIC).
source: Purification and proteomic analysis identified Non-stop as part of a CP190/Nup98/Sgf11/e(y)2/mdg4 protein complex, termed Non-stop identity complex (NIC), that is essential for maintenance of EC identity.
evidence: Proteomic analysis identified the components of the NIC complex.

claim: NIC is essential for maintenance of EC identity.
source: Purification and proteomic analysis identified Non-stop as part of a CP190/Nup98/Sgf11/e(y)2/mdg4 protein complex, termed Non-stop identity complex (NIC), that is essential for maintenance of EC identity.
evidence: Genetic experiments showed that RNAi of NIC subunits resulted in loss of EC identity.

claim: Non-stop protects NIC proteins from age-dependent decline.
source: In part, Non-stop protects NIC proteins from age-dependent decline, safeguarding the EC-gene expression signature, as well as large-scale nuclear organization in these cells, preventing premature aging.
evidence: Experiments showed that maintaining Non-stop levels prevented decline of NIC subunits in aged ECs.

claim: Non-stop safeguards the EC-gene expression signature.
source: In part, Non-stop protects NIC proteins from age-dependent decline, safeguarding the EC-gene expression signature, as well as large-scale nuclear organization in these cells, preventing premature aging.
evidence: RNA-seq data showed that Non-stop is required for expression of EC-related genes.

claim: Non-stop safeguards large-scale nuclear organization in ECs.
source: In part, Non-stop protects NIC proteins from age-dependent decline, safeguarding the EC-gene expression signature, as well as large-scale nuclear organization in these cells, preventing premature aging.
evidence: Microscopy data showed that Non-stop is required for proper nuclear organization in ECs.

claim: Non-stop prevents premature aging.
source: In part, Non-stop protects NIC proteins from age-dependent decline, safeguarding the EC-gene expression signature, as well as large-scale nuclear organization in these cells, preventing premature aging.
evidence: Loss of Non-stop in young ECs phenocopied aged ECs, and maintaining Non-stop levels suppressed aging phenotypes.

claim: Over lifespan, Non-stop protein levels in ECs declined.
source: Over lifespan, Non-stop protein levels in ECs declined, leading to loss of NIC subunits.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showed reduced Non-stop protein levels in aged ECs.

claim: Decline in Non-stop protein levels leads to loss of NIC subunits.
source: Over lifespan, Non-stop protein levels in ECs declined, leading to loss of NIC subunits.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showed reduced NIC subunit protein levels in aged ECs.

claim: Decline in Non-stop is associated with loss of gut identity and physiology at the cellular and tissue levels.
source: This decline is associated with loss of gut identity and physiology at the cellular and tissue levels.
evidence: Multiple assays showed loss of EC identity markers and gut integrity in aged midguts.

claim: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop prevented loss of the NIC.
source: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop prevented loss of the NIC and prevented aging of the gut.
evidence: Overexpression experiments showed that maintaining Non-stop levels prevented decline of NIC subunits.

claim: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop prevented aging of the gut.
source: Maintaining youthful levels of Non-stop prevented loss of the NIC and prevented aging of the gut.
evidence: Multiple assays showed that maintaining Non-stop levels suppressed aging phenotypes.

claim: A collection of RNAi transgenic flies targeting 362 evolutionarily conserved Ub/UbL-related genes were screened.
source: To identify EC identity supervisors, a collection of RNAi transgenic flies targeting 362 evolutionarily conserved Ub/UbL-related genes were screened (Figure 1—source data 2; List of Ubiquitin-Related Genes according to DRSC - http://www.flyrnai.org/DRSC-SUB.html).
evidence: The screen methodology is described in the manuscript.

claim: Genes were knocked-down in fully differentiated ECs of 2–4 day old adult Drosophila females using UAS-RNAi lines and EC-specific conditional driver MyoIA-Gal4/Gal80ts coupled system.
source: Genes were knocked-down in fully differentiated ECs of 2–4 day old adult Drosophila females using UAS-RNAi lines and EC-specific conditional driver MyoIA-Gal4/Gal80ts coupled system (termed MyoIAts; see methods for specific lines used; Salmeron et al., 1990; Brand and Perrimon, 1993; Flint Brodsly et al., 2019).
evidence: The screen methodology is described in the manuscript.

claim: Conditional RNAi was achieved by shifting flies to 29°C for 48 hr.
source: Conditional RNAi was achieved by shifting flies to 29°C for 48 hr for the indicated time, after which guts were dissected and analyzed.
evidence: The screen methodology is described in the manuscript.

claim: Immunofluorescence was used to score loss of proteins which are hallmarks of EC identity.
source: Immunofluorescence was used to score loss of proteins which are hallmarks of EC identity (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The screen methodology is described in the manuscript and illustrated in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Among the changes upon loss of EC identity is the ectopic expression of the ISC marker Delta on the surface of ECs-like polyploid cells.
source: Among the changes upon loss of EC identity is the ectopic expression of the ISC marker Delta on the surface of ECs-like polyploid cells.
evidence: This is a phenotype observed in the screen and described in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of EC identity may be accompanied with a decline in the expression of a GFP signal that is expressed only in fully differentiated ECs.
source: This change may be also accompanied with a decline in the expression of a GFP signal that is expressed only in fully differentiated ECs (derived from the MyoIAts Gal4, UAS-GFP transgene).
evidence: This is a phenotype observed in the screen and described in the manuscript.

claim: Knockdown of seventeen genes resulted in loss of EC identity and appearance of EC-like polyploid cells (PPCs).
source: Knockdown of seventeen genes (Figure 1—source data 2), resulted in loss of EC identity and appearance of EC-like polyploid cells (PPCs).
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: The screen identified three categories of supervisors: 1. EC-specific identity regulators 2. Genes that are required for differentiated cell identity (both EEs and ECs) 3. Genes that are required for identity of all cell types (general identity regulators).
source: Based on cell-specific secondary tests, we identified three categories of supervisors; 1. EC-specific identity regulators 2. Genes that are required for differentiated cell identity (both EEs and ECs) 3. Genes that are required for identity of all cell types (general identity regulators).
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: A group of genes (CG1490; CG2926; CG4080) whose elimination in EEs resulted in a loss of EC, but not EE, identity, acting as inductive identity regulators.
source: Of specific interest were a group of genes (CG1490; CG2926; CG4080) whose elimination in EEs resulted in a loss of EC, but not EE, identity, acting as inductive identity regulators.
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: The effect of genes (CG1490; CG2926; CG4080) on ECs likely involves cell~cell communication via diffusible factors.
source: Likely their effect on ECs involves cell~cell communication via diffusible factors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that elimination in EEs affects ECs.

claim: Among the genes identified were E3 ubiquitin ligases, E2 enzymes, SUMO-related enzymes and ubiquitin-specific peptidases (DUB/USPs).
source: Among the genes identified were E3 ubiquitin ligases, E2 enzymes, SUMO-related enzymes and ubiquitin-specific peptidases (DUB/USPs).
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data.

claim: Nuclear proteins harboring PHD domains that serve as bind to methylated histones, but may confer ubiquitin ligase activity present in ubiquitin ligases were identified.
source: We also identified nuclear proteins harboring PHD domains that serve as bind to methylated histones, but may confer ubiquitin ligase activity present in ubiquitin ligases (Examples are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: The screen results are described in the manuscript with supporting data and examples shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H.

claim: RNAi mediated knockdown of Non-stop in ECs using three independent UAS-RNAi lines resulted in the inability of ECs to maintain MyoIA>UAS-GFP signal followed by ectopic expression of the ISC marker Delta on the surface of EC-like polyploid cells in both females and males.
source: RNAi mediated knockdown of Non-stop in ECs using three independent UAS-RNAi lines resulted in the inability of ECs to maintain MyoIA>UAS-GFP signal followed by ectopic expression of the ISC marker Delta on the surface of EC-like polyploid cells in both females and males (Figure 1C and D, quantitated in 1G and Figure 1—source data 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–J).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1C, D, G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–J.

claim: Non-stop was discovered as a ubiquitin protease essential for axonal guidance in the visual system.
source: Non-stop was discovered as a ubiquitin protease essential for axonal guidance in the visual system (Martin et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Non-stop is required for deubiquitinating monoubiquitinated histone H2B (H2Bub) and activation of gene expression.
source: and it is required for deubiquitinating monoubiquitinated histone H2B (H2Bub) and activation of gene expression (Weake et al., 2008; Mohan et al., 2014; Morgan et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Non-stop is expressed in all midgut cells.
source: Immunofluorescence revealed that Non-stop is expressed in all midgut cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Non-stop is the major H2Bub deubiquitinase in Drosophila.
source: Non-stop is the major H2Bub deubiquitinase in Drosophila, therefore functional loss of Non-stop should lead to an increase in H2Bub levels (Weake et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2008; Morgan et al., 2016; Mohan et al., 2014; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: ECs lacking Non-stop exhibited more H2Bub.
source: Indeed, ECs lacking Non-stop exhibited more H2Bub, and accordingly protein extracts derived from these midguts were characterized by an over 6-fold increase in H2Bub compared to control knockdown midguts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F–H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence and Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F–H.

claim: Protein extracts derived from midguts where Non-stop was knocked down in ECs were characterized by an over 6-fold increase in H2Bub compared to control knockdown midguts.
source: Indeed, ECs lacking Non-stop exhibited more H2Bub, and accordingly protein extracts derived from these midguts were characterized by an over 6-fold increase in H2Bub compared to control knockdown midguts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F–H).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F–H.

claim: Non-stop knockdown in ECs resulted in an increase in Prospero positive cells (likely EEs).
source: We noticed that Non-stop knockdown in ECs resulted in an increase in Prospero positive cells (likely EEs) (Figure 1E,F, and quantified in 1H, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E, F, H.

claim: Reduction of Non-stop in EEs did not impact EE or EC identity or number, and there was no change in Delta expression.
source: However, reduction of Non-stop in EEs did not impact EE or EC identity or number, and there was no change in Delta expression.
evidence: Experimental data described in the manuscript.

claim: Non-stop function in maintaining differentiated identity was confined to ECs and not EEs.
source: Thus, indicating that Non-stop function in maintaining differentiated identity was confined to ECs and not EEs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2I–L).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2I–L.

claim: Non-stop has a role in the biology of progenitor cells.
source: While we focused on differentiated midgut cells, we observed that Non-stop has also a role in the biology of progenitor cells.
evidence: Experimental observations described in the manuscript.

claim: UAS-RNAi-mediated loss of Non-stop in progenitors (derived by the Esg>Gal4 driver that is expressed in both ISCs and EBs), resulted in increased progenitor number (Delta positive small cells).
source: UAS-RNAi-mediated loss of Non-stop in progenitors (derived by the Esg>Gal4 driver that is expressed in both ISCs and EBs), resulted in increased progenitor number (Delta positive small cells).
evidence: Experimental data described in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of Non-stop in progenitors resulted in mis-differentiation of progenitors as evident by polyploid cells that ectopically express Delta, as well as GFP under the control of the Esg>Gal4 driver.
source: It also resulted in mis-differentiation of progenitors as evident by polyploid cells that ectopically express Delta, as well as GFP under the control of the Esg>Gal4 driver (Figure 1—figure supplement 2M–N).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2M–N.

claim: Targeting of Non-stop only in ISCs in the gut (using Delta>Gal4), resulted in lethality at the pupal stage with no viable adults.
source: Targeting of Non-stop only in ISCs in the gut (using Delta>Gal4), resulted in lethality at the pupal stage with no viable adults.
evidence: Experimental observation described in the manuscript.

claim: Elimination of Non-stop in EBs using Hey>Gal4 had no impact on the gut tissue.
source: In contrast, elimination of Non-stop in EBs using Hey>Gal4 had no impact on the gut tissue, (Figure 1—figure supplement 2O–P, and not shown).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2O–P.

claim: Non-stop elimination affected the entire midgut tissue; resulting in ectopic activation of the Notch pathway.
source: At the tissue level, Non-stop elimination affected the entire midgut tissue; resulting in ectopic activation of the Notch pathway, as well as the stem-cell enhancer M5-4 esg::LacZ in polyploid cells, indicating that these cells were losing their differentiated state (Figure 1I–L, quantified in 1Q, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1I–L, Q.

claim: Non-stop elimination resulted in ectopic activation of the stem-cell enhancer M5-4 esg::LacZ in polyploid cells, indicating that these cells were losing their differentiated state.
source: At the tissue level, Non-stop elimination affected the entire midgut tissue; resulting in ectopic activation of the Notch pathway, as well as the stem-cell enhancer M5-4 esg::LacZ in polyploid cells, indicating that these cells were losing their differentiated state (Figure 1I–L, quantified in 1Q, and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1I–L, Q.

claim: Loss of Non-stop resulted in increased phospho-Histone H3 which is indicative of mitotic activity in small cells, likely progenitors.
source: Loss of Non-stop also resulted in increased phospho-Histone H3 which is indicative of mitotic activity in small cells, likely progenitors (Figure 1M,N).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1M, N.

claim: Knockdown of Non-stop in ECs reduced epithelial integrity as evidenced by leaking of blue colored food outside the gut.
source: Knockdown of Non-stop in ECs reduced epithelial integrity as evidenced by leaking of blue colored food outside the gut, and reduced overall survival (Figure 1O,P and R respectively; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1O, P, R.

claim: Knockdown of Non-stop in ECs reduced overall survival.
source: Knockdown of Non-stop in ECs reduced epithelial integrity as evidenced by leaking of blue colored food outside the gut, and reduced overall survival (Figure 1O,P and R respectively; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1R.

claim: G-TRACE is a dual-color GAL4-dependent system, that enables tracing fully differentiated non-dividing cells.
source: G-TRACE is a dual-color GAL4-dependent system, that enables tracing fully differentiated non-dividing cells (Figure 2A; Evans et al., 2009; Flint Brodsly et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a description of the G-TRACE system, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The MyoIA-Gal4/Gal80ts directs the expression of the color system only to fully differentiated ECs.
source: In brief, the MyoIA-Gal4/Gal80ts directs the expression of the color system only to fully differentiated ECs.
evidence: This is a description of the G-TRACE system used in the study.

claim: Expression of the Gal4 is dependent on the EC-specific MyoIA promoter that induces expression of a UAS-RFP (red).
source: Expression of the Gal4 is dependent on the EC-specific MyoIA promoter that induces expression of a UAS-RFP (red).
evidence: This is a description of the G-TRACE system used in the study.

claim: Gal4 activity induces the expression of a Flp-recombinase resulting in a recombination event that drives permanent expression of a GFP regardless of the differentiation state of the cell.
source: Concomitantly, this Gal4 activity induces the expression of a Flp-recombinase resulting in a recombination event that drives permanent expression of a GFP regardless of the differentiation state of the cell.
evidence: This is a description of the G-TRACE system used in the study.

claim: Wildtype young ECs express both RFP and GFP, and are the only population of polyploid cells (PPCs), observed in control midgut tissue.
source: Therefore, wildtype young ECs express both RFP and GFP, and are the only population of polyploid cells (PPCs), observed in control midgut tissue (Figure 2B).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In guts where Non-stop was knocked-down in ECs, other populations of fluorescently colored PPC's were observed.
source: In contrast, in guts where Non-stop was knocked-down in ECs, other populations of fluorescently colored PPC's were observed.
evidence: Experimental data described in the manuscript.

claim: PPCs that express only GFP, termed PPC** (PPCGFP+ RFP-) were observed in guts where Non-stop was knocked-down in ECs.
source: These include PPCs that express only GFP, termed PPC** (PPCGFP+ RFP-; Figure 2C, and quantified in 2J; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2C, J.

claim: PPC** did not express EC-related transcription factors such Odd-skipped and exhibited reduced expression of the differentiated lamin, LamC.
source: Unlike control cells, PPC** did not express EC-related transcription factors such Odd-skipped and exhibited reduced expression of the differentiated lamin, LamC (Figure 2D–G).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2D–G.

claim: A small number of PPC** that express the ISC marker Delta (<%1) were observed.
source: We observed a small number of PPC** that express the ISC marker Delta (<%1; Figure 2H,I).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2H, I.

claim: PPC** are likely ECs that were no longer fully differentiated, failing to maintain EC identity.
source: By the nature of the G-TRACE system, we concluded that these PPC** are likely ECs that were no longer fully differentiated, failing to maintain EC identity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the G-TRACE system and experimental observations.

claim: PPCs that did not express EC key transcription factors such as Pdm1 and caudal were observed.
source: In accordance, PPCs that did not express EC key transcription factors such as Pdm1 and caudal were also observed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Guts where Non-stop was targeted in ECs were populated with PPCs lacking expression of either RFP or GFP (termed PPC*).
source: In addition, guts where Non-stop was targeted in ECs were populated with PPCs lacking expression of either RFP or GFP (termed PPC*), and are likely mis-differentiated progenitors that failed to activate the myo-promoter and the entire RFP/GFP marking system, and 30% of these cells ectopically expressed Delta (Figure 2H–J, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2H–J.

claim: PPC* are likely mis-differentiated progenitors that failed to activate the myo-promoter and the entire RFP/GFP marking system.
source: In addition, guts where Non-stop was targeted in ECs were populated with PPCs lacking expression of either RFP or GFP (termed PPC*), and are likely mis-differentiated progenitors that failed to activate the myo-promoter and the entire RFP/GFP marking system, and 30% of these cells ectopically expressed Delta (Figure 2H–J, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the G-TRACE system and experimental observations.

claim: 30% of PPC* cells ectopically expressed Delta.
source: In addition, guts where Non-stop was targeted in ECs were populated with PPCs lacking expression of either RFP or GFP (termed PPC*), and are likely mis-differentiated progenitors that failed to activate the myo-promoter and the entire RFP/GFP marking system, and 30% of these cells ectopically expressed Delta (Figure 2H–J, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2H–J.

claim: The phenotypes observed upon acute loss of Non-stop are highly similar to the ones observed in aged midguts.
source: The phenotypes observed upon acute loss of Non-stop are highly similar to the ones observed in aged midguts (Figure 2K–R; Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 2K–R and Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: G-TRACE analysis of aged ECs established that the aged midgut (5 weeks old) are populated with ECs that are no longer differentiated (PPC**).
source: G-TRACE analysis of aged ECs established that the aged midgut (5 weeks old) are populated with ECs that are no longer differentiated (PPC**), as well as mis-differentiated progenitors (PPC*).
evidence: Experimental data described in the manuscript.

claim: The aged midgut (5 weeks old) are populated with mis-differentiated progenitors (PPC*).
source: G-TRACE analysis of aged ECs established that the aged midgut (5 weeks old) are populated with ECs that are no longer differentiated (PPC**), as well as mis-differentiated progenitors (PPC*).

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The elimination of Progerin by expression of Smurf2 in HGSP-fibroblasts reduced the deformation observed in these cells.
source: The elimination of Progerin by expression of Smurf2 in HGSP-fibroblasts reduced the deformation observed in these cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Enhancing Progerin degradation by inhibiting the human ortholog of Non-stop, USP22, will restore nuclear architecture, and suppress the premature aging phenotypes observed in HGPS cells.
source: Thus, it is possible that enhancing Progerin degradation by inhibiting the human ortholog of Non-stop, USP22, will restore nuclear architecture, and suppress the premature aging phenotypes observed in HGPS cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the role of Non-stop in maintaining nuclear organization.
